question: If a chord subtends an angle of 75° at the center, the angle it subtends at the circumference on the same side is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By the circle theorem, the angle subtended by a chord at the center is exactly twice the angle it subtends at the circumference.

Angle at center = 75°

Angle at circumference = Angle at center ÷ 2

Angle at circumference = 75° ÷ 2 = 37.5°

**∴ The correct answer is 37.5°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Angle subtended by the chord at the center = 75°

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Angle at center = 2 × Angle at circumference on the remaining part of the circle.
